methods.label: Bound the largest side
methods.explanation:
Write the positive integer side lengths in order as \(a\le b\le c\). This prevents counting different orderings of the same sides separately. Since the perimeter is \(7\), the triangle inequality gives
\[
7-c=a+b>c,
\]
so \(c<3.5\) and hence \(c\le3\). If \(c\le2\), all three sides would be at most \(2\), giving perimeter at most \(6\). Therefore \(c=3\).

Now \(a+b=4\), with \(1\le a\le b\le3\). The only possibilities are \((a,b)=(1,3)\) and \((2,2)\), producing
\[
(1,3,3)\quad\text{and}\quad(2,2,3).
\]
Both satisfy the triangle inequality. By SSS, each side triple determines one triangle up to congruence, and the different side triples give non-congruent triangles. Thus there are \(\boxed{2}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: A triangle-inequality bound reduces the problem to listing two small integer possibilities.
